newsitem.title: FRANCE: Several analysts cut Peugeot estimates.
newsitem.headline: Several analysts cut Peugeot estimates.

text.p: Several analysts have cut their earnings estimates for the PSA Peugeot Citroen group in 1997 and 1998, after the French carmaker posted disappointing results for 1996 and said there was no sign of a let-up in the price competition in Europe.
Analysts said the stock was overvalued and that Peugeot was less well-equipped than others to face difficult European market conditions.
The main debate among analysts was on whether the group would remain profitable this year.
"The market is split between those who think the group will remain profitable in 1997 and those who don't," said CRP analyst Olivier Pouteau.
On April 17 Peugeot said its 1996 profits fell by 57 percent to 734 million francs as a fierce price war raged in the French market.
This was well below analysts' estimates ranging from 800 million to 1.7 billion francs.
Asked if Peugeot would be profitable during 1997, chairman Jacques Calvet told a news conference on Thursday that this was the objective.
"Are we 100 percent sure? The answer is no," he said.
French brokerage Du Bouzet changed its recommendation on Peugeot from strengthen to reduce.

In a report to investors it also cut its estimates for earnings per share for 1997 to 5.60 francs from a previous target of 18.80 francs. It reduced its forecast for 1998 earnings per share to 28.20 francs from 31.50 francs.
Margin deterioration was such that it might prevent Peugeot from reaching a 1998 earnings level sufficient to return to the average European price earnings ratio for the sector, it also said.
IMI Sigeco changed its recommendation to sell from hold and cut its estimates for 1997 earnings per share to a net loss of three francs from a previous estimate of a profit of 24 francs.
It is now targeting 1998 EPS of 16 francs against 42 francs previously.

Cheuvreux de Virieu remains a seller on Peugeot and has cut its forecast for 1997 EPS to a net loss of seven francs from a profit of 32.50 francs. It now expects 1998 EPS of 21.60 francs against 48.30 francs previously.
CPR cut its estimate for net profit to 700 million francs from a previous target of one billion for 1997 and to 2.5 billion francs from 3.0 billion for 1998.

Analyst Olivier Pouteau said that favourable exchange rates in Europe and the good performance of the industrial vehicles branch should allow Peugeot to remain profitable in 1997 despite a poor environment.
"1997 will be very difficult to manage with a decline in the French market and a price war that we think will last," he said, maintaining his recommendation at "reduce".
Credit Suisse First Boston said it cut EPS estimates for Peugeot to 11.3 francs from 22.3 francs for 1997 and to 20.4 francs from 34.6 francs for 1998.
Transbourse, which surprised some when it predicted in February a loss of three billion francs for 1997, said it was expecting most analysts to revise downwards their estimates on Peugeot.
There will be a presentation for analysts in London on April 21.
Peugeot was down 3.93 percent to 587 francs at 1555 GMT.
